newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has decided to trim its 984-billion-baht budget for fiscal year 1997 by 2.4 percent to 959 billion baht because it will fall short of its revenue collection target. Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda has attributed the anticipated revenue shortfall to the economic slowdown which has prompted the government to readjust the budget. (THE NATION)

- Newin Chidchob and his team of seven former members of parliament have left Chart Thai Party to join Muan Chon Party of Justice Minister Chalerm Yubamrung. The justice minister says Newin set no conditions regarding financial support, nor positions within the party or a future Cabinet, should Muan Chon form part of the next government. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The Palang Dharma Party, whose leader Thaksin Shinawatra is skipping the Nov 17 election to concentrate on political reform, has hinted that it will push for a constitutional change to the rule that reserves the premiership for members of parliament only. Leading the street campaign is Chamlong Srimuang, former party leader who is still a respected figure in the party.

- Property developer Ban Chang Group Plc plans to reduce its property investments over the next 2-3 years due to faltering real estate market. The company says it will instead turn its attention to investments in infrastructure and power generation projects. (MANAGER)

- The Bank of Thailand is ready to disclose in-depth information on off-shore banking activities to banks' parent agencies as part of international cooperation agreements, but the information should be kept confidential. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government will take steps today to fully liberalise imports of raw materials used in animal feed. The move is intended to help livestock producers reduce their costs, which will make Thai exports more competitive. (BANGKOK POST)
